states.dynasty_note: Kublai Khan, Great Khan and Emperor Shizu of Yuan (1260-94). The crown prince Zhenjin died in 1286; his son Temür succeeds in 1294.

summary.en: The old Kublai rules all of China; his campaigns against Japan, Vietnam and Java have failed or are being prepared.
summary.de: Der greise Kublai beherrscht ganz China; seine Feldzüge gegen Japan, Vietnam und Java sind gescheitert oder in Vorbereitung.

states.dynasty_note: King Chungnyeol, son-in-law of Kublai; Goryeo is a Yuan vassal.
Emperor Fushimi reigns in Kyoto; power lies with the Kamakura bakufu, the shogun prince Hisaaki and the regent Hōjō Sadatoki. Kyushu is guarded against a third Mongol invasion.

ruler.name: Sakya hierarchs and dpon-chen under the Yuan

states.dynasty_note: Tibet is governed for the Yuan by the Sakya school and its administrators (dpon-chen); the Drikung rising was crushed in 1290.
The Khalji took the throne in June 1290 after the last Mamluk (Slave) sultan. The Mongols of the Chagatai raid the Punjab.
Balban's son Bughra Khan rules Bengal as an independent sultan; his son Kaykaus succeeds c.1291.
The Soomra dynasty of lower Sindh (Ismaili tradition).
Hindu kings of Kashmir (the sultanate dates from 1339); names around 1290 uncertain.
Vaghela king of Gujarat (1275-96); conquered by the Khalji in 1299.
The declining Paramara kingdom, divided between rival claimants.
Hammira repulses Jalal al-Din's attacks (1290-92).
Ramachandra (1271-1311), raided by Ala al-Din Khalji in 1296.
Prataparudra succeeded his grandmother Rudramadevi (d. c.1289).
At the height of the later Pandyas (1268-1310); Marco Polo visits the coast in 1292. Venad and the Kerala coast are attached through the spread.
Pandya armies sacked Yapahuwa (1284) and took the Tooth Relic; the throne is uncertain until Parakramabahu III (1302).
Aryacakravarti kings, vassals of the Pandya.
Victor over the third Mongol invasion (Bạch Đằng, 1288).
Che Man, king from 1288.
Angkor under Jayavarman VIII (1243-95), paying tribute to Kublai since 1285. Lavo (Lopburi) is in its sphere.
Ram Khamhaeng (c.1279-98) has extended his overlordship to the Malay peninsula (Nakhon Si Thammarat).
Mangrai took Hariphunchai (Lamphun) in 1281/92; Chiang Mai is founded only in 1296.
The remnant of the Pagan empire after the Mongol invasion (1287); the three Myinsaing brothers hold Kyaukse.
Wareru proclaimed himself king at Martaban in 1287 (Pegu taken c.1287-96).
Kertanegara (1268-92), who sent the Pamalayu expedition to Sumatra (1275) and mutilated Kublai's envoys (1289); Majapahit rises from his fall (1292-93).
Melayu at Dharmasraya, heir to Srivijaya, under Singhasari overlordship since the Pamalayu expedition.
The first Muslim ruler on Sumatra (d. 1297); Marco Polo calls at Samudra in 1292.
The Tepanec of Azcapotzalco, a rising lordship (its hegemony comes in the 14th century).
The great Mississippian centre, past its peak and losing people; abandoned by c.1350.
The early Inca kingdom of Cusco, one of several Andean chiefdoms (rulers before Pachacuti are legendary).
Přemyslid king since 1278 (ruling himself since 1290). Kłodzko came to him at Henry IV Probus' death (1290); in 1291 he takes Kraków and becomes duke there.

summary.en: Silver from Kutná Hora and a claim on Kraków: Wenceslaus II is about to reach for the Polish crown.
summary.de: Silber aus Kuttenberg und ein Anspruch auf Krakau: Wenzel II. greift nach der polnischen Krone.

coa.blazon: Gules, a lion rampant double-queued argent crowned or

states.dynasty_note: Albert I, Duke of Austria and Styria since 1282, son of King Rudolf I. He also manages the Habsburg lands in Swabia and the Aargau.
Prince-archbishopric; Archbishop Rudolf of Hoheneck (1284-90) died in August 1290; the see is contested between his successor Stephan of Lower Bavaria and Konrad of Fohnsdorf (1291).

coa.blazon: Per pale or, a lion sable, and gules, a fess argent

name.en: Duchy of Upper Bavaria and Rhine Palatinate
name.de: Herzogtum Oberbayern und Pfalzgrafschaft bei Rhein

states.dynasty_note: Wittelsbach duke of Upper Bavaria and Count Palatine of the Rhine, elector.
Wittelsbach duke of Lower Bavaria (later King of Hungary 1305).

coa.blazon: Argent, a moor's head couped proper crowned gules
Gules, two keys in saltire argent

states.dynasty_note: Burgrave of Nuremberg, a loyal ally of Rudolf I.

coa.blazon: Or, a lion sable within a bordure compony argent and gules
Per pale or, a demi-eagle sable, and bendy gules and argent
Per fess dancetty gules and argent

states.dynasty_note: Bamberg also holds Villach and lands in Carinthia.

coa.blazon: Or, a lion sable, overall a bend argent
Or, a hen sable on a mount vert

states.dynasty_note: Count since 1279, a persistent opponent of Rudolf I's revindications.

coa.blazon: Or, three stag antlers fesswise sable
Per bend gules and vert, a morning star or
Argent, a cross sable, a chief gules
Per pale gules and argent, a pine cone or

states.dynasty_note: Imperial city since 1218; besieged twice by Rudolf I in 1288-89 and forced to submit, still an imperial city.
Imperial city (Reichsfreiheit 1218).
Count Palatine of Burgundy; in 1291 he betroths his daughter Joan to a son of Philip IV (Treaty of Évreux 1295 hands the county to France).

coa.blazon: Azure billetty or, a lion or

states.dynasty_note: Humbert I of La Tour-du-Pin, Dauphin through his wife Anne (1282). An imperial fief until it is sold to France in 1349.
Defeated and captured at Worringen (1288); the city of Cologne is free of him since.
Archchancellor of Germany; he will crown Adolf of Nassau in 1292.

coa.blazon: Argent, a chief gules charged with three crowns or

states.dynasty_note: Count of Berg, victor at Worringen with Brabant; raised Düsseldorf to a town in 1288.

coa.blazon: Argent, a lion gules crowned azure
Gules, an inescutcheon argent, an escarbuncle or
Or, a fess chequy gules and argent

states.dynasty_note: Count Adolf of Nassau, elected King of the Romans in May 1292.

coa.blazon: Azure billetty or, a lion or

states.dynasty_note: Ottonian line of Nassau.

coa.blazon: Azure billetty or, a lion or
Or, a lion gules crowned azure

states.dynasty_note: Landgrave of Hesse since the separation from Thuringia (1264); raised to imperial prince in 1292.

coa.blazon: Azure, a lion barry argent and gules crowned or
Gules, a key argent with a mullet or
Azure crusily, a lion argent crowned or

states.dynasty_note: Duke of Saxony at Wittenberg, son-in-law of Rudolf I; claims the Saxon electoral vote.

coa.blazon: Barry of ten sable and or, a crancelin vert in bend

ruler.name: John II, Albert III and Eric I

states.dynasty_note: The sons of John I of Saxony rule jointly (divided 1296).

coa.blazon: Barry of ten sable and or, a crancelin vert in bend

name.en: Margraviate of Meissen and Landgraviate of Thuringia

states.dynasty_note: Margrave of Meissen (1288/89-91) and of Landsberg and Lower Lusatia; dies August 1291.
Albert the Degenerate at the Wartburg, at war with his sons Frederick and Dietrich; sells the landgraviate to Adolf of Nassau in 1294.

coa.blazon: Per pale argent and barry sable and or, an eagle gules dimidiated
Per pale argent and barry sable and or, an eagle gules dimidiated

states.dynasty_note: The Ascanian margraves rule jointly in two lines (Otto IV and his kin; Otto V the Long). Upper Lusatia and Stargard belong to them.

coa.blazon: Or semé of hearts gules, a lion azure

states.dynasty_note: The three sons of Albert I the Tall; the partition into Grubenhagen, Göttingen and Wolfenbüttel takes effect during 1291.

coa.blazon: Gules, two lions passant guardant or

states.dynasty_note: Archbishop Eric (1283-95), a brother of the Brandenburg margraves.
Count Otto III (r. 1249-1306); the county passes to Jülich-Berg only in 1346. Herford itself is an imperial abbey and town under the counts' protection.
Noble lords of Lippe; Simon I rules from 1273/75 to 1344.

coa.blazon: Gules, two keys in saltire argent
Gules, two keys in saltire argent

states.dynasty_note: Henry I has been a prisoner in Cairo since 1271 (released 1298); his son Henry II governs. A duchy only from 1348.

coa.blazon: Or, a bull's head sable crowned gules

states.dynasty_note: Lordship of Rostock (to Denmark 1300, to Mecklenburg 1323).

ruler.name: Henry I and Nicholas II of Werle

coa.blazon: Argent, a bull's head sable crowned or

states.dynasty_note: House of Griffins: Bogislaw IV with his brothers Barnim II and Otto I (partition of 1295).

coa.blazon: Azure, a griffin segreant gules crowned or

states.dynasty_note: The last Samborid; by the Treaty of Kępno (1282) Pomerelia passes to Przemysł II of Greater Poland at his death (1294).
Prince Wizlaw II, a Danish vassal; Stralsund is his town.
The Frisian freedom: self-governing rural districts (Ostergo, Westergo, the Ommelanden, Emsland, Rüstringen) under elected judges.
Pope Nicholas IV (Girolamo Masci, the first Franciscan pope), 1288-92. Romagna is under papal rectors since 1278; the Comtat Venaissin papal since 1274.

summary.en: Nicholas IV preaches a new crusade for Acre and backs the Angevins against Aragonese Sicily.
summary.de: Nikolaus IV. predigt einen Kreuzzug für Akkon und stützt die Anjou gegen das aragonesische Sizilien.

coa.blazon: Gules, two keys in saltire Or and argent beneath a papal tiara

states.dynasty_note: House of Anjou. King of Sicily without the island; also Count of Provence and Forcalquier, overlord of Achaea, and lord of Corfu and the Albanian coast at Kanina and Butrint.

coa.blazon: Azure semé-de-lis Or, a label gules

states.dynasty_note: House of Barcelona: James, second son of Peter III, King of Sicily since 1285; heir of Aragon (from June 1291). Roger of Lauria holds Djerba and the Kerkennah islands (1284).

coa.blazon: Per saltire Or paly gules and argent an eagle sable

states.dynasty_note: Judicate of Arborea.
Doge since November 1289. Crete, Modon and Coron are Venetian colonies; Negroponte is ruled by Lombard triarchs under a Venetian bailo; Ragusa has a Venetian count.

coa.blazon: Azure, a winged lion passant Or holding a book

ruler.name: Captains of the People (Oberto Spinola, Corrado Doria)

states.dynasty_note: Commune under two Ghibelline captains of the people. Victor over Pisa at Meloria (1284). Pera (Galata) since 1267; Caffa is modelled as its own city. The Doria hold Alghero and Castelgenovese in Sardinia; Sassari is a commune in the Genoese orbit.
Ghibelline commune, captain of war Guido da Montefeltro (1289-93); holds Cagliari and Gallura in Sardinia.
Guelph commune; victor at Campaldino (11 June 1289).
Guelph commune under the government of the Nine (from 1287).

coa.blazon: Per fess argent and sable (the Balzana)

states.dynasty_note: Guelph commune.
Ghibelline commune, defeated at Campaldino.
Guelph commune within the Papal States.

coa.blazon: Argent, a griffin rampant gules crowned Or

states.dynasty_note: Montefeltro lordship.

coa.blazon: Bendy Or and azure, a chief Or with an eagle sable
Azure, three towers argent on three peaks vert

states.dynasty_note: Guelph commune (the Pepoli lordship comes only in 1337).

ruler.name: Ottone Visconti, archbishop; Matteo Visconti, captain of the people

states.dynasty_note: Archbishop Ottone Visconti rules Milan since 1277; his great-nephew Matteo is captain of the people (1287) and becomes imperial vicar in 1294.

coa.blazon: Argent, a serpent azure crowned Or devouring a child gules

states.dynasty_note: Scaliger lordship (since 1277).

coa.blazon: Gules, a ladder argent ensigned with an imperial eagle sable

states.dynasty_note: Bonacolsi lordship; Pinamonte is deposed by his son Bardellone later in 1291.

coa.blazon: Barry of six Or and sable

states.dynasty_note: Este lordship; Modena (1288) and Reggio (1289) accepted Obizzo as lord.

coa.blazon: Azure, an eagle argent crowned Or

states.dynasty_note: Free commune ruling Vicenza (the Carrara lordship begins only in 1318).
Ghibelline commune, its parties led by the counts of Langosco and the Beccaria; free again after William VII of Montferrat lost his lordship in 1290.
Alberto Scotti, Guelph merchant-banker, made himself lord (dominus) of Piacenza in 1290.
Guelph commune; the Correggio lordship begins only in 1303.
Guelph commune (the Cavalcabò lordship comes later).
Guelph commune ruling its contado and Valcamonica.
Commune divided between the Suardi (Ghibelline) and the Colleoni (Guelph).
Commune ruled by its parties (Rusca and Vitani); Bellinzona and Lugano belong to it.
Commune under the Guelph Vistarini and Fissiraga families.
Commune; out of the Montferrat lordship since 1290. Vercelli, its own commune, is joined to it here (gap).
Wealthy commune of merchant-bankers, leader of the league against William VII of Montferrat.
Commune that took William VII of Montferrat prisoner in September 1290 and keeps him caged until his death in 1292. Tortona, its ally, is joined to it here (gap).
Guelph commune in Florence's orbit.
Commune beside its bishop; San Gimignano, a free commune of its own, is joined here (gap).
The da Camino lordship of Treviso, Feltre and Belluno (1283-1312).
Patriarch of Aquileia (1273-99), lord of Friuli.
Albert II, brother of Meinhard II, holds Gorizia, the Puster valley and Istrian lordships (division of 1271).
Meinhard II, Count of Tyrol, Duke of Carinthia since 1286, holds Carniola and the Windic March in pledge from the Habsburgs; father-in-law of Albert of Austria. Controls the bishopric of Trent.

coa.blazon: Argent, an eagle gules crowned or

states.dynasty_note: William VII, the Great Marquis, has been held in an iron cage by the Alessandrians since September 1290 (dies February 1292); his son John I acts.
Count since 1285; Turin and Pinerolo are held by his nephew Philip of Savoy under him (the principality of Piedmont/Achaea dates from 1294-1301). Bresse through his marriage to Sibylle of Baugé.

The last Árpád, crowned 23 July 1290 after Ladislaus IV was murdered. Charles II of Naples claims the crown for his son Charles Martel; the great lords (Kőszegi, Csák, Aba, Šubić) act almost on their own.

coa.blazon: Per pale: barry gules and argent; azure semé-de-lis Or

states.dynasty_note: The former Serbian king Dragutin rules Mačva, Belgrade (1284), Usora and Soli as a vassal of Hungary.
Banate of Bosnia under Hungarian overlordship; Usora and Soli belong to Dragutin.

coa.blazon: Azure, a bend argent between fleurs-de-lis Or

states.dynasty_note: Romanian voivodes south of the Carpathians under Hungarian overlordship. Litovoi fell fighting Hungary c. 1277-1279; his brother Bărbat was captured, ransomed himself and accepted Ladislaus IV as overlord. No ruler is attested between Bărbat and Thocomerius (c. 1310); the ruler of 1 January 1291 is unknown (the Negru Vodă founding of 1290 is later legend). Comes Laurentius of Câmpulung is attested 1300.

coa.blazon: Azure, an eagle Or holding a cross

states.dynasty_note: King since 1282; took Skopje (1282) and northern Macedonia from Byzantium. Zeta and Hum belong to the realm.
Commune under a Venetian count.
Tsar since 1280, tributary to Nogai of the Golden Horde (his son Theodore Svetoslav is a hostage there); he flees to Byzantium in 1292.

coa.blazon: Gules, a lion rampant Or crowned

states.dynasty_note: Despot Shishman, a Cuman-Bulgarian lord, vassal of Nogai.
Andronikos II (1282-1328). The Anatolian frontier is crumbling under the Turkmen; Durazzo was recovered from the Angevins in 1288; the Zaccaria hold Phocaea under the emperor.

coa.blazon: Gules, a cross Or between four betas Or

states.dynasty_note: Despotate of Epirus; allied with the Angevins against Byzantium.
The sons of the sebastokrator John I Doukas (d. c.1289), Constantine and Theodore, under their mother Hypomone.
Princess since 1289 with her husband Florent, vassals of Charles II of Naples.
Duke since 1287 under the regency of his mother Helena Angelina Komnene; Argos and Nauplia, Salona and Bodonitsa are fiefs of the duchy.

coa.blazon: Per saltire Or paly gules and argent with eagles sable (Aragon-Sicily)

states.dynasty_note: Duchy of the Archipelago (Naxos) under Venetian protection.

Henry II of Cyprus, crowned King of Jerusalem at Tyre in 1286. The Hospitallers, Templars and Teutonic Knights hold quarters and castles (Atlit, Tortosa, Sidon's sea castle). Acre falls on 18 May 1291, the rest by August.

summary.en: The last crusader coast. Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil is gathering the army that will besiege Acre in April.
summary.de: Die letzte Kreuzfahrerküste. Sultan al-Aschraf Chalil sammelt das Heer, das im April Akkon belagern wird.

states.dynasty_note: House of Lusignan.
Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, vassal of the Ilkhan.

coa.blazon: Or, a lion rampant Gules crowned

states.dynasty_note: House of Estridsen. Eric VI, king since 1286 (murder of Eric V at Finderup), rules with the support of his mother Agnes of Brandenburg; northern Estonia is a Danish duchy.

coa.blazon: Or semé of hearts gules, three lions passant azure crowned or

states.dynasty_note: Duke of South Jutland (Schleswig), of the line of King Abel.
House of Bjälbo. Birger succeeds his father Magnus Ladulås (d. 18 December 1290) as a boy of ten; the marshal Torgils Knutsson governs.

House of Sverre. Eric II, the "priest-hater"; his daughter Margaret, heiress of Scotland, died in Orkney in autumn 1290. Iceland since 1262-64, Greenland, the Faroes, Orkney, Shetland, Jämtland and Bohuslän belong to the realm.

coa.blazon: Gules, a lion rampant or crowned, holding an axe argent

ruler.name: Burchard von Schwanden (Grand Master, resigned 1290); Konrad von Feuchtwangen from 1291

states.dynasty_note: The Order has subdued Prussia (last rising 1283) and holds Kulmerland; the Grand Master still sits in Acre (Venice from 1291, Marienburg from 1309). Memel belongs to the Livonian branch.

coa.blazon: Gules, the Lamb of God argent

states.dynasty_note: The Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order; Semigallia surrendered in 1290 after the destruction of its hillforts.

coa.blazon: Argent, a cross sable, a sword gules

states.dynasty_note: The archbishop and the city of Riga, increasingly at odds with the Order (open war from 1297).

coa.blazon: Gules, a cross and a crozier in saltire argent
Gules, a key and a sword in saltire argent

states.dynasty_note: Grand Duke Butvydas succeeds his brother Butigeidis (d. c.1290/91); Samogitia and Black Ruthenia (Navahrudak, Grodno) belong to the realm.
Princes in the Lithuanian orbit; poorly documented before 1307.

name.en: Duchy of Greater Poland and Kraków

states.dynasty_note: Piast duke of Greater Poland, heir of Pomerelia (Kępno 1282), duke of Kraków since 1290; leaves Kraków to Wenceslaus II during 1291 and is crowned King of Poland in 1295.
Władysław Łokietek holds Sandomierz (1289-92), Sieradz and Brześć Kujawski; later King of Poland (1320).
Bolesław II of Płock with his brother Konrad II of Czersk (reunited 1294); Łęczyca (Casimir II) is attached here.
Henry V of Legnica took Wrocław at the death of Henry IV Probus (1290).
Henry III of Głogów; claimant to Wrocław and later to Greater Poland.

coa.blazon: Or, an eagle sable with a crescent argent on its breast

states.dynasty_note: Mieszko I of Cieszyn and Oświęcim (division of 1290 with Racibórz).
Casimir of Bytom, the first Silesian duke to do homage to Wenceslaus II (1289).
Republic; the princes it invites are those of Vladimir.

coa.blazon: Argent, two bears sable supporting a throne

states.dynasty_note: The Lithuanian-born prince Dovmont defends Pskov (1266-99).
Grand Prince of Vladimir (1283-93) from his own appanage of Pereslavl, protected by Nogai against his brother Andrey.
Andrey of Gorodets, backed by Khan Tokhta, takes the grand principality in 1293.
A small appanage of the youngest son of Alexander Nevsky; Kolomna is still Ryazan's (taken 1301).

coa.blazon: Gules, Saint George on horseback argent
Gules, a throne with a crown or

states.dynasty_note: With his brother Konstantin of Uglich. Veliky Ustyug on the Sukhona belongs to the Rostov princes.
Fyodor Rostislavich, a favourite at the Horde; also prince of Smolensk.

coa.blazon: Argent, a bear sable holding an axe
Azure, two fish in saltire argent
Or, a prince with a sword gules

states.dynasty_note: Lev I, son of King Daniel, rules Galicia from Lviv; Lublin he lost again in 1289. Tributary to the Horde (Nogai).
Prince of Volhynia since 1289 (death of Volodymyr Vasylkovych); Lutsk is attached here only through the spread.
Under Tatar baskaks; its princes are not reliably known.

Khan Talabuga (1287-91) rules the right (western) wing; the left wing east of the Ural, the ulus of Orda, is held by Köchü (Konichi) under him. Talabuga is overthrown by Nogai and his protégé Tokhta during 1291.

The beklerbek Nogai, great-grandson of Jochi, rules the western steppe from the Dnieper to the Danube and makes and unmakes khans; Bulgaria and Vidin pay him tribute. His faith: he is said to have accepted Islam, his ulus is largely shamanist.
Genoese colony under Tatar suzerainty since c.1266.
Eastern Georgia under Ilkhanid overlordship; Vakhtang II installed by the Ilkhan after the execution of Demetrius II (1289).

coa.blazon: Argent, a cross gules between four crosses gules

states.dynasty_note: Western Georgia, independent of the Mongols, under David VI Narin; Mingrelia (Odishi) and Abkhazia are its fiefs.
Atabeg of Samtskhe, a direct vassal of the Ilkhan.
John II, married to the emperor's daughter Eudokia (1282), the first to style himself "Emperor of the East".
Bahri Mamluk sultan since November 1290 (death of his father Qalawun on the march against Acre).

summary.en: Al-Ashraf Khalil has sworn to finish his father's work: Acre will be besieged in April.
summary.de: Al-Aschraf Chalil hat geschworen, das Werk seines Vaters zu vollenden: im April wird Akkon belagert.

coa.blazon: Or, a cup Gules between two inscriptions Sable

charges.text: Glory to our lord the Sultan

states.dynasty_note: The last Ayyubid principality, vassal of the Mamluks.
Sharifs of Mecca under Mamluk suzerainty; Medina has its own Husaynid emirs, attached here.
Rasulid sultan since 1250, at the height of the dynasty; took Zafar in Dhofar (1279).
Nabhani maliks of inner Oman; Qalhat and the coast stand under Hormuz.
The kings of Old Hormuz on the mainland (the move to Jarun island c.1300), tributary to the Ilkhan.
Ilkhan Arghun (1284-91), a Buddhist who sought an alliance with the Latin West against the Mamluks; he dies on 10 March 1291. Islam becomes the state faith only under Ghazan (1295).
Sultan since 1282/84 under Ilkhanid governors; real power lies with the Mongol officers and the Turkmen begs.
Karamanid beylik in the Taurus, at war with the Seljuks and the Ilkhanids.
The strongest beylik of the west, raiding the Byzantine frontier.
Turkmen beylik on the Carian coast; took Tralles from Byzantium (1282-84).
Descendants of the vizier Sahib Ata Fakhr al-Din Ali (d. 1288), lords of Afyonkarahisar (1275-1341).
The sons of the pervane Mu'in al-Din Süleyman (d. 1277) hold Sinop (1277-1322).

name.en: Beylik of the Chobanids of Kastamonu

states.dynasty_note: Frontier begs of Kastamonu since the early 13th century (the Candarids replace them c.1292-1309).
Turkmen lords of Denizli (Ladik), 1262-1368.
Lords of Beyşehir (1285-1326).
Osman, son of Ertuğrul, a frontier chief on the Bithynian border; the beylik is only counted from c.1299.
Kart maliks of Herat, vassals of the Ilkhan.
The Qara Khitai dynasty of Kerman under Ilkhanid overlordship (1222-1307).
Du'a, khan of the Chagatai ulus (1282-1307), the junior partner of Qaidu.
Qaidu, grandson of Ögedei, the paramount power of Central Asia and Kublai's enemy (1269-1301).
Marinid sultan since 1286; Algeciras, Tarifa, Gibraltar and Ronda are his Andalusian bridgeheads.
The Banu al-Azafi rule the trading city of Ceuta (1249-1327), recognising the Marinids.
Zayyanid sultan (1283-1304), besieged by the Marinids from 1299.
Hafsid caliph at Tunis (1284-95); the west of the realm (Bijaya, Constantine) has broken away under his nephew.
Separate Hafsid realm of Bijaya and Constantine since 1285.
The freed slave Sakura, a general who seized the throne (c.1285-1300), extends Mali to Gao.
Sayfawa kings of Kanem; ruler names around 1290 are uncertain.
Son of Yekuno Amlak, founder of the Solomonic dynasty (1270); reigns 1285-94.

coa.blazon: Vert, a lion Or bearing a cross

states.dynasty_note: The Walashma took Ifat and ended the Makhzumi sultanate of Shewa in 1285.
King Shemamun, fighting Mamluk-backed rivals for the throne of Dongola.
The Mahdali sultans (from c.1277) control the gold trade of Sofala.
Oba Oguola (c.1280-95), who walled Benin City by tradition.
House of Plantagenet. Queen Eleanor of Castile died on 28 November 1290. Edward I is Lord of Ireland, Duke of Aquitaine and, for his son, holds Ponthieu.

summary.en: Edward I has conquered Wales and sits as arbiter of the Scottish succession after the death of the Maid of Norway.
summary.de: Eduard I. hat Wales erobert und soll nach dem Tod der Maid von Norwegen über die schottische Thronfolge entscheiden.

coa.blazon: Quarterly, 1 and 4 Azure semé-de-lis Or (France ancient), 2 and 3 Gules three lions passant guardant Or (England)

ruler.name: Guardians of Scotland (William Fraser, Robert Wishart, John Comyn, James the Steward)

states.dynasty_note: Interregnum: Margaret, Maid of Norway, died in Orkney in autumn 1290. Thirteen claimants; Edward I is asked to judge (the Great Cause, Norham 1291).

summary.en: Scotland has no king. The Guardians must choose between Balliol and Bruce, with Edward I of England as arbiter.
summary.de: Schottland hat keinen König. Die Guardians müssen zwischen Balliol und Bruce wählen, mit Eduard I. von England als Schiedsrichter.

coa.blazon: Or a lion rampant within a double tressure flory-counter-flory Gules

states.dynasty_note: Uí Néill; the kingship is disputed between Domnall mac Briain and the Mac Lochlainn line.

coa.blazon: Argent a sinister hand couped at the wrist Gules (the Red Hand)

states.dynasty_note: Ó Domhnaill kings of Tír Chonaill.

coa.blazon: Or issuing from the sinister a cross Gules

states.dynasty_note: The O'Conor kingship is reduced to the Shannon plain around Roscommon; the de Burgh earls of Ulster hold most of Connacht as lords of Connacht under the English crown.

coa.blazon: Argent an oak tree eradicated Vert

states.dynasty_note: Ó Briain kings of Thomond, contesting Thomas de Clare's lordship of Bunratty.

coa.blazon: Gules three lions passant guardant in pale per pale Or and Argent

states.dynasty_note: MacCarthy kings of Desmond.
Mac Murchadha Caomhánach kings of Leinster in the Wicklow and Wexford uplands.
House of Capet. Philip IV rules jure uxoris Navarre and Champagne. Anjou and Maine were given to his brother Charles of Valois in 1290.

summary.en: The young Philip the Fair consolidates the royal domain and eyes Gascony and Flanders.
summary.de: Der junge Philipp der Schöne festigt die Krondomäne und hat Gascogne und Flandern im Blick.

states.dynasty_note: House of Dreux (Montfort-l'Amaury branch of the Capetians). John II is also Earl of Richmond in England.
House of Dampierre. Guy also holds the march of Namur in the Empire. Saint-Omer and Béthune belong to Artois (Robert II of Artois) and are left to France in the spread; see borders rules.
Elder Capetian house of Burgundy.

coa.blazon: Bendy of six Or and Azure, a bordure Gules

states.dynasty_note: Beatrice, lady of Bourbon, married to Robert of Clermont, son of Saint Louis. Raised to a duchy only in 1327.

coa.blazon: Azure semé-de-lis Or, a bend Gules

states.dynasty_note: Queen Joan I and her husband Philip IV; Navarre is governed by French governors.

coa.blazon: Quarterly, 1 and 4 Gules a cross saltire and orle of chains Or (Navarre), 2 and 3 Azure semé-de-lis Or a bend compony Argent and Gules (Évreux)

name.en: County of Foix and Viscounty of Béarn

states.dynasty_note: Roger-Bernard III of Foix inherited Béarn from his father-in-law Gaston VII Moncada (d. April 1290).

coa.blazon: Quarterly, 1 and 4 Or three pallets Gules (Foix), 2 and 3 Or two cows passant Gules (Béarn)

states.dynasty_note: Counts of Armagnac and Fezensac.

coa.blazon: Quarterly, 1 and 4 Argent a lion Gules (Armagnac), 2 and 3 Gules a lion passant guardant Or (Rodez)
Gules four otelles in saltire Argent
Gules three lions Or armed, langued and crowned Azure

states.dynasty_note: John I won the duchy of Limburg at Worringen (5 June 1288).

coa.blazon: Sable a lion rampant Or armed and langued Gules

states.dynasty_note: Count of Holland and Zeeland; West Friesland subdued 1289.

coa.blazon: Quarterly, 1 and 4 lozengy Argent and Azure (Bavaria), 2 and 3 Or a lion rampant Gules (Holland)
Quarterly, 1 and 4 Or a lion rampant Sable, 2 and 3 Or a lion rampant Gules

states.dynasty_note: Count (the duchy dates from 1339). Lost the Limburg succession at Worringen 1288.

coa.blazon: Azure a lion rampant queue fourchée Or

states.dynasty_note: Prince-bishopric (Oversticht and Nedersticht).

coa.blazon: Or a fess chequy Argent and Gules (La Marck)

states.dynasty_note: Held by Guy of Dampierre, count of Flanders, since 1263.

coa.blazon: Or a lion rampant Sable, over all a bendlet Gules
Barry of ten Or and Gules

states.dynasty_note: Count since his father Henry VI fell at Worringen (1288); later King of the Romans and Emperor.

coa.blazon: Barry argent and azure, a lion rampant gules crowned or, tail forked
Or, on a bend gules three alerions argent

states.dynasty_note: County; a duchy only from 1354.

coa.blazon: Azure semé of crosses crosslet fitchy or, two barbels addorsed or

states.dynasty_note: House of Burgundy (Ivrea). Sancho IV, the Brave, prepares the siege of Tarifa (taken October 1292).

summary.en: Sancho IV wants the Strait: the Marinid bridgeheads of Tarifa and Algeciras.
summary.de: Sancho IV. will die Meerenge: die merinidischen Brückenköpfe Tarifa und Algeciras.

coa.blazon: Quarterly, 1 and 4 Gules a castle Or (Castile), 2 and 3 Argent a lion rampant Purpure (León)

states.dynasty_note: House of Barcelona. Alfonso III, the Liberal, took the Balearics from his uncle James II of Majorca (1285-87); excommunicated, he negotiates the Treaty of Tarascon (February 1291). He dies on 18 June 1291.
James II of Majorca has lost the islands to Aragon (1285-87) and keeps Roussillon, Cerdanya and the lordship of Montpellier under French protection.
House of Burgundy. Denis, the Farmer King, founded the university at Lisbon (1290).

coa.blazon: Argent five escutcheons Azure each charged with bezants Argent, a bordure Gules charged with castles Or

states.dynasty_note: Nasrid dynasty. Málaga came back from the Banu Ashqilula through the Marinids in 1279, Guadix in 1288.

coa.blazon: Gules a bend Or engouled by dragons' heads, charged with the motto 'wa-la ghaliba illa Allah'

name.en: Siege of Acre and the end of the crusader states
name.de: Belagerung von Akkon und das Ende der Kreuzfahrerstaaten

name.en: Aragonese Crusade (War of the Sicilian Vespers)
